summary: Verified JS fix in admin/index.html: getLenientAttribute helper correctly extracts partyName across namespace variants. Served static admin dashboard via python http.server on :8765 (Java backend not running - out of scope). Tested 3 CPA XML variants via file upload flow using data-testid selectors. All party names rendered correctly, no '(onbekende partij)' fallback observed. cpaId out-of-scope behavior confirmed unchanged as instructed.
critical_code_review_comments: getLenientAttribute helper is correctly namespace-agnostic (uses attr.localName with fallback to split(':')). Case-insensitive match works. Fix is minimal and safe.

Out of scope but noted: cpaId, Status@value, PartyId@type, Endpoint@uri, Certificate use similar namespaced-attribute lookups that would benefit from the same helper. Per user instruction NOT flagged as a bug in this iteration; can be addressed in a future pass if desired.

renderNetworkMap fallback: when only 1 party exists, it duplicates the same party as both sender & receiver (targets = [sender]). This is a pre-existing behavior, not a regression - visible in cpa2/cpa3 screenshots.
seed_data_creation: Created /tmp/cpa1.xml (no ns), /tmp/cpa2.xml (tp: prefix), /tmp/cpa3.xml (cpa: prefix) as test CPA XMLs.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Java backend was not built/started (no JDK/Maven in pod). Tested static admin/index.html by serving via `python3 -m http.server 8765` from /app/ebms-adapter/ebms-orchestrator/src/main/resources/static and interacting with data-testid=tab-cpa-button + #fileInput + data-testid=cpa-party-node-*. The partyName fix (getLenientAttribute at line ~321) works for no-prefix, tp: prefix, and arbitrary cpa: prefix.
rca of the issue: Original code used p.getAttribute('tp:partyName') || p.getAttribute('partyName') || p.getAttribute('PartyName'), which is a hardcoded prefix list and misses any other namespace prefix. Fix introduces getLenientAttribute() iterating element.attributes and matching by localName case-insensitively, correctly handling all namespace prefixes.
